newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down, Central Bank sets pace.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down, Central Bank sets pace.

text.p: * Peso hits day-low of 26.245 to the dollar
The Philippine peso finished weaker on Friday at 26.243 from 26.235, pulled down by the Central Bank's lower trading range, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.239 to the dollar from 26.235. Volume was higher at $134 million from $128.90 million.
"It was the Central Bank who instigated the move,"a dealer said. The Central Bank quoted a bid and offer rate for the dollar at 26.235 and 26.25 versus the prior day's 26.232 and 26.245.
Dealers said banks were bent on selling their dollars due to the weak demand for it.
But when the Central Bank quoted its desired range, that triggered the buying of dollars, sending the peso to a day-low of 26.245, dealers said.
"The Central Bank was an aggressive buyer. It seems it wants to build up its reserves further," the same trader said.
He estimates the Central Bank may have purchased $13 million at 26.233 for same-day delivery.
